subject: SLA attribution proposal for recent filter/toolcall failures
messages:
From: Sam Walsh <sam.walsh@novushealth.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Thu, 18 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Intermittent content filter failures impacting tool-calls — request for SLA attribution

Hi Diego,

We started seeing a pattern of failures late yesterday (2027-02-17 ~17:30 UTC) where Redwood's content filter / tool-calling path rejected or truncated tool calls from our production 'clinical-summarize' route. Symptoms we observed:
- ~12 distinct incidents over an 8 hour window where the tool-call returned 4xx/timeout instead of the expected JSON payload.
- Latency spikes on successful calls (~+2.0–2.5s median) and a ~5% overall error rate for that route during the window.
- Several cases where structured output was malformed (missing fields) leading to downstream ingestion failures.

We attached the diagnostic logs we collected (diagnostic_logs_20270217.zip). This is customer-facing; some providers saw degraded UX and one escalation from a hospital partner.

We need two things from Redwood ASAP:
1) A short-term remediation and mitigation plan we can ship to our ops team (preferably something we can flip on per-route).
2) A proposal for SLA attribution or a credit for the impacted window while you investigate.

Please escalate on your side — happy to hop on a quick call. We are also going to loop in procurement/legal if there is going to be a formal amendment.

Thanks,
Sam Walsh
Head of Integrations, NovusHealth
sam.walsh@novushealth.com

Attachment: diagnostic_logs_20270217.zip

From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Sam Walsh <sam.walsh@novushealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Feb 2027 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Intermittent content filter failures impacting tool-calls — request for SLA attribution

Hi Sam — thanks for the heads up and for sending the logs. I’m really sorry NovusHealth hit this in production.

I’ve looped in Marissa (AE) and Karthik (product/security) and Evelyn from support. Initial read: the errors look like aggressive filter scoring on a small subset of messages that also triggers our tool-call fallback path, which in some permutations returns an HTTP error instead of the expected structured payload.

Immediate next steps from our side (I’ll own coordination):
- Rapid mitigation: we can enable a per-route fallback policy that attempts an alternative filter profile (less aggressive) for up to three retry attempts. This is a configuration change and does not require code changes.
- We’ll run a targeted tuning session on your 'clinical-summarize' route and share a monitoring dashboard with 1-min granularity.
- Karthik will advise on the safety/redistribution risk of a less aggressive filter.

I’ll follow up today with a formal short-term remediation + a proposed attribution/credit approach. If you can confirm the list of affected customers (or a count of impacted requests) that will help us size the credit.

Diego
Account Lead, Redwood Inference

Subject: Fwd: Intermittent content filter failures — internal proposal

Team — forwarding Sam's note. Draft bridge proposal below; need immediate take/edits because Sam wants an offer to present to procurement by EOD tomorrow.

Draft SLA attribution / bridge play (short-term, 7d window):
- Technical mitigations (immediate): enable per-route less-aggressive filter profile + 3x retry with backoff for 'clinical-summarize'. Share dashboard (1-min granularity) and an alert channel for incidents.
- Operational (monitoring): build temporary dashboard filtered to NovusHealth route, include token-level error breakdown and tool-call success rate.
- Compensation (one-time): apply a one-time service credit equal to 5% of Feb invoice for NovusHealth, capped at $12,000.
- Governance: require ProcureIT legal sign-off on a short amendment that states the credit is attributionary (not admission of breach) and documents the 7-day bridge period.
- Post-incident: deliver root-cause analysis (RCA) within 7 business days and a remediation timeline for long-term fix (kernel/tuning or model policy change).

Questions / notes:
- Karthik: is the less-aggressive profile safe for clinical content? Any red-team concerns we should list in the amendment?
- Marissa: can we approve the credit cap/legal ask? This is likely below our standard deal-adjustment threshold but we should confirm.
- Evelyn: please prepare a one-page dashboard snapshot we can hand to Sam and procurement.

Karthik, Marissa — ping me if you want different numbers (credit %) or a longer bridge. I’d prefer a short bridge + RCA rather than an open-ended SLA carve-out.

Thanks,
Diego

Date: Fri, 19 Feb 2027 09:30:00 -0800
Subject: Proposed SLA attribution and 7-day bridge plan for NovusHealth

Hi Sam — following our investigation, here is the formal proposal for a short-term bridge while we complete the RCA and follow-on fixes. Please review and reply to accept so we can get procurement involved and enact the changes immediately.

Summary (SLA Attribution Play — 7 day bridge):
1) Technical mitigations (effective within 2 hours of acceptance):
   - Per-route fallback: for the 'clinical-summarize' route we will enable an alternate, less-aggressive filter profile with up to 3 automatic retries and exponential backoff. This reduces the chance of tool-call rejections that were observed.
   - Monitoring: we will stand up a temporary dashboard (1-min granularity) showing tool-call success rate, median latency, and error taxonomy for your route. We will share view-only access.
2) Compensation: one-time service credit equal to 5% of your February 2027 invoice, capped at $12,000 (applied to the next billing cycle).
3) Governance & timeframe: bridge window = 7 calendar days from acceptance. During the window we will take the following actions: RCA delivered within 7 business days; proposed permanent remediation plan within 14 days.
4) Legal: we will require ProcureIT to countersign a brief amendment clarifying that applying the credit is attributionary and not an admission of breach. We will prepare the amendment and share a DocuSign link.

Attachments: sla_matrix_review.pdf (high-level spreadsheet mapping route -> SLO -> mitigation)

If you accept, please reply and we’ll get the amendment to ProcureIT and flip the per-route fallback immediately. If you prefer a different credit structure or a longer bridge, tell us and we’ll adjust.

Thanks again — we take this seriously and want to make sure your production traffic is stable.

Diego Fernandez
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
diego_fernandez@redwood.com
